claim_label: Coupling of NiTi Superelasticity, Inter-Wire Friction, Pressure, and Bending Stiffness
claim_text_original: Coupling among NiTi superelastic response, inter-wire slip/friction, pressure and bending stiffness remains open.
claim_text_normalized: Coupled mechanics governing how stress-induced phase transformation, inter-wire stick-slip contact, and external confinement pressure interact to determine composite bending stiffness and hysteresis.
why_potentially_novel: At mentor proposal and early V001, coupling four physical domains (superelastic phase transformation, inter-wire contact, external fluid pressure, and beam bending stiffness) was hypothesized to require a new micromechanical constitutive-contact theory.
search_conducted: MP1-V001 and MP1-V002 targeted searches on SMA cables, hysteretic damping, and frictional multiwire assemblies.

strongest_prior_art_threat.paper_title: Nonlinear Vibration Absorber with Pinched Hysteresis: Theory and Experiments
strongest_prior_art_threat.what_source_actually_proves: Demonstrates that assemblies containing Nitinol wires under cyclic bending directly exhibit pinched hysteresis and amplitude-dependent stiffness caused by simultaneous inter-wire friction and martensitic phase transformation.
strongest_prior_art_threat.what_source_does_not_prove: Does not apply an independently controlled external radial confinement pressure.

source_records.paper_title: Nonlinear Vibration Absorber with Pinched Hysteresis: Theory and Experiments
source_records.what_source_actually_proves: Simultaneous inter-wire friction and phase transformation produce pinched hysteretic bending response.
source_records.what_source_does_not_prove: Does not modulate pressure as an active control parameter.

source_records.paper_title: Mechanical response of single and double-helix SMA wire ropes
source_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2022-Mechanical response of single and double-helix SMA wire ropes.pdf
source_records.what_source_actually_proves: Directly couples 3D Auricchio SMA constitutive model with Coulomb friction contact formulation in Abaqus.
source_records.what_source_does_not_prove: Does not evaluate actively pressurized straight wire bundles in bending.

source_records.paper_title: NiTi SMA Superelastic Micro Cables: Thermomechanical Behavior and Fatigue Life under Dynamic Loadings
source_records.what_source_actually_proves: Inter-filament friction causes self-heating, which shifts phase transformation stresses via Clausius-Clapeyron.
source_records.what_source_does_not_prove: Does not apply active fluid confinement.

claim_before: Coupling among NiTi superelastic response, inter-wire slip/friction, pressure, and bending stiffness is an unaddressed novel mechanics domain.
claim_after: Coupling is partially pre-empted by existing NiTi-contact literature; survives only as an empirical hypothesis testing whether existing models predict pressure-controlled bending.
reason_for_change: Prior literature (Carboni 2016, Vahidi 2022, Silva 2022) already couples NiTi transformation with inter-wire contact and friction. Combining standard NiTi constitutive laws with standard Coulomb contact naturally produces coupled response without requiring a new constitutive law.
scientific_consequence: C7 cannot be claimed as a 'proven novel coupling theory'; it must be formulated as a model-discrimination question testing whether existing frameworks fail under active pressure.
feasibility_impact: Requires local diagnostic instrumentation (DIC, FBG, thermal imaging) to separate phase transformation from friction and avoid parameter compensation.
pivot_relevance: Forms the ultimate surviving scientific core of MP1 after all architectural and material claims were stripped away.
historical_interpretation: Open in V001 (S04); substantially pre-empted in early V002 (S06); challenged by Astra (S10); remediated in Stage 3 (S12) into a model-discrimination hypothesis.
superseded_interpretation: Belief that the coexistence of 4 physical factors in one device demonstrated an unformulated branch of mechanics.
corrected_interpretation: Coupling naturally emerges from standard constitutive + contact equations; empirical testing must verify if standard models break down before claiming novelty.
